samples.description: Shared 1988–2002 Table 1 and Table 2 firm-year pool from domestic standard consolidated industrial annual Compustat statements with a unique valid dated CCM/CRSP security, nonfinancial fiscal-year SIC, current/prior actual assets in the same observed CURCD, and pooled 1% tail trimming of observed financial-statement ratios other than special items. The SAS handoff retains the Table 1 pool and a common Table 2 equation (6) eligibility flag; Table 2 additionally requires one-year-ahead earnings in the observed matching currency and actual next-year assets, or a verified performance-delisting substitution using the latest annual book equity and asset observations dated on or before the event; a t+1 statement dated after the event is not used.

assumptions: Contemporaneous ratios use average assets (AT_t + AT_{t-1})/2; the source does not identify the averaging dates.

Actual Earnings_{t+1} uses average assets (AT_{t+1} + AT_t)/2 only when the t+1 assets and currency are observed. A missing t+1 IBC is replaced only after a dated CRSP performance delisting in the actual t-to-t+1 window. For that replacement, I use the latest annual book-equity and asset observations dated on or before DLSTDT; when the observed t+1 balance sheet is dated after delisting, the replacement uses current-year CEQ and current-period average assets. The paper leaves the exact dates unspecified, so this is an event-date best-effort rule.

Performance-related CRSP delistings are coded as DLSTCD 500 or 520–584, following the standard Shumway classification because the paper does not enumerate codes. Annual bottom-decile ranks use the common Table 2 sample and SAS ties=mean ranking.

The Table 2 note's inclusive SI cutoff (SPI/average assets <= -0.02) governs over the equation (5) prose's strict threshold. OLS uses conventional default standard errors because no correction is reported.

limitations: Table 2 does not specify the precise average-assets dates, the book-equity reporting date for delisted firms, or the CRSP delisting-code set. The explicit best-effort choices and event dates are documented in design.md and the SAS aggregates.
The regression template uses two-sided p-values and 10%, 5%, and 1% star levels; the paper's Table 2 legend uses 5% and 1% significance levels only.
